findings.claim: The freshness gate is HONESTLY RED today: served corpus rag/corpus/h22_nodes.json is 22.0.368-stamped while the ratified build is 22.0.400, so check_corpus_stamp_fresh ok:false (STALE) and K.7 verdict FAIL. This is the observed-vs-asserted gap the leg closes (recon Finding 5: corpus guarded at build time, unguarded downstream), working as designed - not a defect. The release is correctly blocked until the corpus is re-ingested/re-stamped to .400.

harness/state/drop.json is gitignored (present in the main working tree, ABSENT from forked worktrees), so it cannot be the sole in-worktree ratified authority. resolve_ratified_build prefers drop.json when present, else the HIGHEST-major committed symbol table's houdini_version (the same authority W4-KNOW target 7 uses in knowledge.py). Both agree at 22.0.400. The authority is chosen independently of the corpus under test, so a downgrade-stamped corpus cannot self-select an older table (regression-tested).

Adversarial crucible surfaced 4 WEAK gaps, ALL FIXED with regression tests: (a) concurrent authorized writes crashed on a shared .tmp (Windows PermissionError) -> unique-temp + bounded os.replace retry = last-writer-wins, 0/8 crashes [criterion A]; (b) a non-dict corpus (JSON list/str/num/bool) raised AttributeError -> checks.py verdict:ERROR -> LLM adjudication instead of a deterministic block -> _read_corpus now rejects non-dict, gate returns ok:false [criterion B]; (c) POLICY_BLOCKED was exact-lowercase membership, so 'APEX'/'Apex'/'apex ' wired passed the pure verify -> case-normalized; (d) the ledger's ratified_build/revision/gate were forgeable by a token-holder -> the GATE now cross-checks ratified_build against resolve_ratified_build (verify_ledger stays pure).

Per-context wiring reality (from the served corpus): cop=358, cop2=132, lop=169 wired @ 22.0.368; sop/top/vop/dop/obj/rop/chop unwired; apex policy-blocked (D-H22-2, never wired locally). The ledger records this honestly and the gate cross-checks it against the corpus so it cannot drift.

for_ruling.claim: Ledger revision anti-rollback is out of scope for a stateless single-file gate: write_ledger stamps a monotone `revision`, but verify_ledger cannot detect a replay to an older-but-valid ledger without an external monotonic anchor (an orchestrator-recorded last-seen revision, or a git-history check). The module docstring discloses this boundary honestly (guarantee = sole-sanctioned-API + tamper-evidence + corpus + ratified_build cross-check, NOT unforgeable/anti-rollback). Recommend: accept as a documented limitation for the solo-localhost posture; escalate to an orchestrator-recorded revision anchor only if a multi-writer/rollback threat becomes real.

The freshness gate is wired as task K.7's verify (release-blocking), NOT a guardrail (the explicit K.5 ruling: a freshness gate run every sprint fails mid-edit). I left the R.R release capstone untouched (minimal blast radius). If the human wants corpus freshness folded into the aggregate release verdict, add corpus_stamp_fresh (or a K.7 reference) to R.R's inputs — an orchestration/human call, not an agent's.
for_ruling.recommend: human decides whether K.7 feeds the R.R capstone

The re-ingest itself is a BUILD leg (held for Joe); this is the probe that scopes it.
